 "K-Pop Concerts Become Tickets to Korea"... A Bold Move to Attract 300,000 Southeast Asian Tourists
 by Kim Heeyun 
 Published 09 Nov.2026 16:09(KST) 
 Share 
 Language 
 Text Size 
 Print 
 KTO partners with Cebu Pacific and Traveloka
Indonesian and Philippine financial firms link payment benefits with visa convenience
Visitors from Indonesia to South Korea up 23.4%; arrivals from the Philippines up 15.6%
 The Korea Tourism Organization is joining forces with Traveloka, one of Southeast Asia's largest online travel agencies (OTAs), to attract 300,000 tourists to South Korea over the next two years. It is also expanding its partnerships to include a Philippine low-cost carrier (LCC) and major local banks, pursuing a strategy that links K-pop concerts, air routes and financial benefits to attract visitors.
 Park Seonghyeok, president of the Korea Tourism Organization (left), and Traveloka co-founder Albert pose for a photo after signing a memorandum of understanding in Jakarta, Indonesia, on the 4th to attract more tourists to South Korea. The two sides plan to jointly attract 300,000 tourists from Southeast Asia to South Korea over the next two years. Korea Tourism Organization
 View original image 
 The Korea Tourism Organization said on November 9 that its president, Park Seonghyeok, signed memorandums of understanding with major local companies to expand the market for travel to South Korea during a visit to Jakarta, Indonesia, and Manila, the Philippines, from November 3 to 7.
 A key part of the effort is cooperation with Traveloka, a major OTA in Southeast Asia. On November 4, the organization signed an MOU with Traveloka and agreed to jointly attract 300,000 tourists to South Korea over the next two years, leveraging the company's local network in five countries, including Singapore and Malaysia. The plan is to convert demand for travel to South Korea into actual bookings and visits through the online travel platform's sales network.
 The organization is also strengthening its cooperation with airlines. On November 6, it signed an agreement with Cebu Pacific, a leading Philippine low-cost carrier. In conjunction with a large-scale K-pop concert scheduled to take place in the Philippines in March 2027, the organization plans to promote travel packages to South Korea, attract independent travelers and boost routes to regional airports in South Korea.
 It is also working to increase demand for travel to South Korea through financial companies. With BCA, Indonesia's largest private bank, it will promote travel to South Korea and offer payment benefits to the bank's cardholders. It will conduct joint marketing with Philippine financial group BDO Unibank to attract family travelers. BDO is also participating in a visa simplification program for travel to South Korea led by the Korean Embassy in the Philippines and the tourism organization, and the organization plans to link visa convenience with financial benefits.
 The Southeast Asian market for travel to South Korea has been growing recently. From January to September this year, 330,629 tourists from Indonesia visited South Korea, up 23.4% from the same period last year. The Philippines was the largest source of visitors among Southeast Asian countries last year, with 615,141 arrivals in South Korea. Visitor numbers from the Philippines through September this year also rose by more than 15.6% year over year.
 The organization plans to combine the sales networks of local travel platforms, airlines' transport networks and financial companies' customer bases to increase demand for travel to South Korea. It will also focus on spreading visitors beyond Seoul and the surrounding metropolitan area to other regions.

 Park Seonghyeok, president of the Korea Tourism Organization, said, "This sales campaign in Southeast Asia is significant because it turned interest in South Korea into actual demand for visits through close cooperation with local companies. Through multifaceted collaboration with global companies, we will increase the number of visitors to South Korea and drive qualitative growth, including sustainable tourism development in regional areas and the creation of high-value demand."
